newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower on hedging, Sparks.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower on hedging, Sparks.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed lower on hedge selling and on bearish input from a Sparks Companies estimate for 1997 U.S. wheat production, traders said.

Traders said Sparks pegged 1997 U.S. total wheat production at 2.531 billion bushels, above USDA's July forecast for 2.431 billion bushels. Also Sparks estimated 1997-98 U.S. wheat ending stocks at 861 million bushels, well above USDA's July forecast for ending stocks at 650 million bushels, traders said.
Benson Quinn sold 1.3 million bushels of September and sold nearly one million bushels of December, traders said.

The first load of new crop spring wheat arrived Tuesday in Minneapolis, a trader said. The wheat was 14.3 percent protein, sixty pound test weight and was from fields around Forman, North Dakota that were yielding 35 bushels to 40 bushels per acre, the traders said.
The market was underpinned by commercial buying with Cargill Inc a buyer of one million September and Continental Grain bought 1.2 million December, traders said.
MGE spring wheat futures closed 3-1/4 to four cents per bushel lower, with September down 3-1/4 at $3.80-3/4.
Spring wheat futures volume was estimated by the MGE at 15,794 contracts, above the 14,907 traded Monday.
Feed barley futures closed unchanged to 0.05 cent per cwt higher, with September unchanged at $6.20 per cwt.
